role: Core of the Apple Health workout importer: the @MainActor struct holding a HealthKitManager, the Candidate value shown in the import list, and the pure policy functions (sport mapping, duplicate-by-start test, step-count->cadence conversion) used by the +Queries and +Rebuild extensions.
types: HealthWorkoutImporter: struct (@MainActor) — imports/rebuilds workouts from Apple Health; extended in +Queries and +Rebuild
HealthWorkoutImporter.Candidate: struct (Identifiable, Sendable, Equatable) — one external HKWorkout offered for import (id = HKWorkout uuid, dates, sport, sourceName, distance, weather)
state: mem:HealthWorkoutImporter.minimumImportableDuration (static 60 s; also the interrupted-stub threshold in +Rebuild)
toplevel: Header comment (7-36) documents that imports carry no RR/RMSSD/SDNN/alpha1, no mean HR/TRIMP/hrTSS, and elevation gain only on rebuild. Instances are constructed by FitnessTabView+DataMenu.swift:77 and AppLaunchRecovery.swift:17 with the dependency HealthKitManager.

units.does: Candidate.duration: endDate minus startDate in seconds.
Maps an HKWorkoutActivityType plus the indoor flag to an Emuqu Sport, or nil when the activity has no Emuqu equivalent (nil = not offered for import).

branches.effect: nil — workout dropped from the candidate list; .trailRun and .airBike are never produced

units.does: True when any archived start time lies within ±300 s (duplicateStartToleranceSec) of `start`; sport is deliberately not compared.
Converts HealthKit step-count windows into (midpoint Date, steps-per-minute) pairs: value / (duration/60), placed at window start + duration/2.

branches.effect: continue; otherwise the window is dropped (avoids divide-by-zero)
emit the pair; otherwise drop the window

units.does: Spreads each step window's steps-per-minute (computed by cadenceSamples(from:), so zero-length, negative and non-finite windows are dropped) across every whole second the window covers inside [start,end], one (Date, rate) pair per second; windows are taken in finestLast order so where they overlap the finest one comes last and wins in the builder's latest-wins per-second map.

branches.effect: continue; otherwise the window contributes nothing

branches.cond: the window's overlap with [start,end] is non-negative
branches.effect: emit one pair per second from the overlap start through its whole-second length; otherwise nothing

units.does: Sorts windows longest first (ties by earlier start), so in a latest-wins fill the shortest (finest) window of any overlap is applied last, independent of HealthKit's result order.

branches.effect: longer first; otherwise earlier start first
